prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 3 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 2 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Meeting Area. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is the red mannequin; Company B Operations Manager is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): One storyboard image arranged two panels across and two down: shot 1 upper left, shot 2 upper right, shot 3 lower left, and the lower-right cell blank. No lettering, numbers or arrows. Company A is a smooth red artist's mannequin of medium height and average build; Company B is a smooth blue artist's mannequin, medium-tall and lean. Paint the room and furniture realistically: cream walls, pale oak table, four taupe upholstered chairs, timber slats, beige carpet and a sheer-covered glazed opening. Soft daytime illumination comes from camera left, balanced with warm ceiling light; maintain a neutral-warm 5000K appearance, restrained beige and oak tones, gentle contrast and controlled highlights throughout.

Geography: The conversation runs left to right along the near side of the round table: Company A stands at Meeting Area left, facing Company B at Meeting Area right. The table and chairs sit farther into the room behind their conversational line. The glazed opening occupies the room's left wall, while the timber slat panel occupies the right-hand section of the rear cream wall. All cameras remain on the near side of the conversation axis. The view toward A includes the glazed opening at frame left; the reverse toward B reveals the rear timber slats at frame right. Neither person changes position.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Standing head height, looking diagonally toward Company A without crossing the conversation axis. Medium close-up with a 65mm lens feel at f/2.8; red mannequin on the left half, with open space to screen right. Background: Softly defocused sheer-covered glazing at frame left and warm cream wall across the centre and right. The table and chairs remain below the crop; the timber slats remain outside frame right. The red mannequin stands on the left half of the panel, its chest angled toward screen right in three-quarter view. Its head is turned screen right toward the blue mannequin's off-frame position and held slightly inclined forward. Both arms hang at its sides, with both empty hands below the lower edge.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Standing head height appropriate to Company B, looking diagonally toward the right-hand standing position from the same side of the axis. Medium close-up with a 65mm lens feel at f/2.8; blue mannequin on the right half, with open space to screen left. Background: Softly defocused cream wall at frame left and centre, with the timber slat panel at frame right. The glazed opening lies outside frame left and supplies the same soft directional light; table and chairs remain below the crop. The blue mannequin stands on the right half of the panel, its chest angled toward screen left in three-quarter view. Its head is turned screen left toward the red mannequin's off-frame position and held level. Both arms rest at its sides, with both empty hands below the lower edge.
PANEL 3 (row 2, column 1) — Standing head height, matching shot 1's common-side angle, 65mm lens feel and f/2.8 medium close-up. Red mannequin remains on the left half with open space to screen right. Background: The same softly defocused sheer-covered glazing remains at frame left, with warm cream wall across the centre and right. Table and chairs remain below the crop, and timber slats remain outside frame right. The red mannequin stands in the same position, its chest angled toward screen right in three-quarter view. Its head is level and turned screen right toward the blue mannequin's off-frame position, with shoulders lowered and relaxed. Both arms hang at its sides, with both empty hands below the lower edge.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
